classification_review_method: Independent read-only re-derivation during T0 Freeze Gate closure. For each of the 18 geo_observations rows in this batch, the joined geo_evidence row (raw_response + citations) was re-evaluated against the frozen §2.2 rules using three checks: (1) Magic Engine mentioned in response text; (2) owned domain magicengine.com.au present in any citation slot or in the response text; (3) prescriptive language ('we recommend' / 'our pick' / 'our recommendation' / 'recommended option' / 'go with' / 'best choice is' / 'you should use|choose|pick|hire') within 80 characters of a Magic Engine mention. Priority rule applied as documented: mention + owned URL resolves to `cited` and outranks `compared`. Generic decision verbs in neutral explanatory prose (e.g. a bare 'choose') were treated as non-prescriptive, matching the documented rule that `recommended` requires the response to prescribe Magic Engine rather than describe it. No provider was called, no measurement re-run, no database write.

classification_review_checks.mention_not_counted_as_citation: Verified. `cited` was asserted only where an owned-domain URL was actually present, not merely where Magic Engine was named. All 4 cited queries (brand_1, brand_2, brand_3, cmp_1) independently showed owned-domain presence; the 14 not_present queries showed no mention at all, so no mention was silently upgraded.
classification_review_checks.described_not_counted_as_recommendation: Verified. Re-derivation found 0 queries meeting the prescriptive-language test, matching the documented `recommended`=0. No describing/citing response was promoted to `recommended`.
classification_review_checks.priority_rule_consistent: Verified. cmp_1 is the only query matching both a comparison-anchor pattern and owned-URL presence; it resolves to `cited` under the documented priority rule, consistent with the doc's `compared`=0.

limitations: Classification was applied through documented manual rules rather than a frozen executable classifier.

The re-derivation described in classification_review_method reimplemented the documented rules independently for audit purposes; it is not a committed, reusable classifier, so T+7/T+14/T+28 rounds still risk method drift until the rules are landed as code.

The prescriptive-language test depends on a finite phrase list. A prescription worded outside that list would be scored non-prescriptive by both the original pass and this review, so `recommended`=0 is 'no match against the documented phrase set', not a proof that no prescription of any wording exists.
